title: Macrophage ILF3 promotes abdominal aortic aneurysm by inducing inflammatory imbalance in male mice

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, transgenic mouse generation: 'ILF3 conditional overexpression mice (ILF3^flox/floxLysMCre^+)' and later 'macrophage-ILF3 knockout mice (ILF3^flox/floxLysMCre^+)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same exact genotype is first defined as overexpression (ILF3^M–Tg) and later as knockout (ILF3^M–KO). Moreover, a floxed allele with LysM-Cre mediates deletion, not overexpression. This makes the central gain-of-function and loss-of-function mouse results internally impossible as described.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results paragraph on IL-10 expression (Fig. 4C / Supplementary Fig. 5A)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Text states IL-6, TNF-α, MCP-1, and IL-10 all 'exhibited a pronounced decrement in ILF3^M-KO mice', but immediately afterward says IL-10 was 'diametrically opposed' to the pro-inflammatory mediators and earlier states IL-10 was intensified by ILF3 deficiency. IL-10 cannot be both decreased and increased in the same group.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results/mechanism summary: 'Collectively, these findings indicate that ILF3 deficiency modulates inflammatory balance by simultaneously inhibiting the NF-κB and Keap1-Nrf2 signaling pathways' versus later 'In summary ... activating Keap1-Nrf2 pathway due to reduced Keap1 expression'.
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The first sentence says ILF3 deficiency inhibits Keap1-Nrf2 signaling; the later sentence and the underlying data (lower Keap1, increased nuclear Nrf2) show ILF3 deficiency activates the Nrf2 pathway. These are opposite conclusions.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 1J legend versus Results scRNA-seq description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Results text says cells were visualized/classified using UMAP, but the Figure 1J legend says ILF3+ macrophages were projected onto a t-SNE plot. These are different dimensionality-reduction plots, so the text and figure describe inconsistent analyses.
